title: Boolean logic: a two-hand control with a guard
summary: Combine AND, NOT and XOR so a press can only be enabled when both hands are on the push buttons and the guard is closed.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Write a condition that is true only when several inputs are true together.
Turn sentences such as "while it is open" and "only one of the two" into Boolean conditions.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/TwoHand.st the three outputs are not yet right. PressEnable must be ON only with LeftHand, RightHand and GuardClosed all ON. GuardLamp must be ON when the guard is open. OneHandWarning must be ON when exactly one hand is on its button.
stages.checkpoint: You can say, for each output, the condition that turns it ON.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict the three outputs at {{t:20}}, {{t:30}}, and {{t:40}} ms. The inputs change every {{t:10}} ms, so work through one step at a time.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:TwoHand.PressEnable=true,TwoHand.GuardLamp=false,TwoHand.OneHandWarning=false@20|PressEnable ON only}} at {{t:20}} ms; {{v:TwoHand.PressEnable=false,TwoHand.GuardLamp=true,TwoHand.OneHandWarning=false@30|GuardLamp ON only}} at {{t:30}} ms; {{v:TwoHand.PressEnable=false,TwoHand.GuardLamp=false,TwoHand.OneHandWarning=true@40|OneHandWarning ON only}} at {{t:40}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program enables the press with either hand, so PressEnable is already ON at {{t:10}} ms with one hand. Give each output its own condition: PressEnable ON only with both hands on their buttons and the guard closed, GuardLamp ON while the guard is open, and OneHandWarning ON while exactly one hand is on its button. Write the statements yourself: the declarations are already there.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named TwoHand and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:20}}, {{t:30}}, and {{t:40}} ms: the press is enabled once, at {{t:20}} ms, and switches off again at {{t:30}} ms when the guard opens.
stages.checkpoint: PressEnable rises at {{t:20}} ms and falls at {{t:30}} ms, and is never ON while GuardLamp is ON.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Try the same condition with OR instead of AND and say which input combination wrongly enables the press. Then write GuardLamp as NOT GuardClosed AND LeftHand: when does the lamp stay dark although the guard is open?
stages.checkpoint: OR enables the press with a single hand, which is exactly what a two-hand control exists to prevent. NOT applies only to GuardClosed, so that lamp lights only while the guard is open and the left hand is on its button.

hints.text: Read the three sentences of the Edit stage one at a time: each one is the whole condition of one output. Then look at the operator the starting program uses for PressEnable.
Write PressEnable := LeftHand AND RightHand AND GuardClosed; GuardLamp := NOT GuardClosed; OneHandWarning := LeftHand XOR RightHand;

faultCases: The starting program enables the press with either hand, so PressEnable is already ON at {{t:10}} ms with one hand.
